name: LTM Ltd
title: LTM Ltd - 540005 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: IT services read: Q4 USD revenue +1.2% QoQ and 8.1% YoY, but no numeric FY27 guidance and margin fell 100bp QoQ to 15.1% on wage hikes; supply signals are absent, so this is a demand-and-pricing story with hedged tone.

summary.headline: LTM Q4 FY26 revenue rose 1.2% QoQ to USD 1.22bn (8.1% YoY) while Q4 operating EBIT margin fell 100bps QoQ to 15.1% on partial wage hikes.
summary.overview: LTM closed FY2026 with revenue of USD 4.76bn (6% USD growth, 5.3% constant currency) and operating EBIT margin of 15.4%, up 90bps. Q4 revenue grew 1.2% QoQ and 8.1% YoY in USD, with order inflow steady at USD 1.7bn, the sixth straight quarter above USD 1.5bn. Q4 margin dipped to 15.1% from 16.1% in Q3 due to a partial wage hike effective 1 January, partly offset by forex. Management introduced the Lakshya'31 five-year strategy (goal to double revenue in five years), a move to four reporting segments from Q1 FY27, and declined to give numeric FY27 guidance.

+10.3% YoY; large deal wins up 300%, including six USD 100mn+ deals
+1.2% QoQ, +8.1% YoY in USD; constant currency +7% YoY; rupee revenue +4.7% QoQ, +15.6% YoY

financial_highlights.change: Basic EPS ex-exceptional Rs 45.4 vs Rs 47.7 in Q3
Stable; sixth consecutive quarter above USD 1.5bn
Up from Rs 13,346 Cr in FY25
DSO vs 85 days in Q3; attrition vs 13.8% in Q3

segments.name: BFSI (FY26 USD growth)
segments.commentary: Grew 3.7% for FY26 despite a decline at the top BFSI account; management said the account's decline was bottomed out in Q4, with recovery slower than the decline.

segments.name: Manufacturing and Resources (FY26 USD growth)
segments.commentary: Grew 12.7% for FY26; being renamed Production from Q1 FY27 to include manufacturing and energy and utilities.

segments.name: Tech, Media and Communication (FY26 USD growth)
segments.commentary: Declined 0.7% for FY26; Q4 recovery attributed to faster-than-expected ramp-up of a few SOWs with a top account in cloud acceleration.

segments.name: Consumer (FY26 USD growth)
segments.commentary: Grew 13.2% for FY26; Healthcare, life sciences and public services (9.6% growth) merged into Consumer for reporting from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Geographies (FY26 USD growth)
segments.commentary: Americas +4.0%, Europe +12.4%, rest of world +11.6%. Management expects Europe to keep outgrowing the Americas.

segments.name: Verticals overall
segments.commentary: Four of five verticals grew double digits YoY in Q4; three of five did so for full FY26.

guidance_outlook: No numeric guidance given; management said it does not guide but is confident of FY27 growth momentum at industry-leading levels, with quarterly softness possible.
Management said there is no reason to believe FY26's growth momentum will not carry into FY27; a 'softness' quarter or two is possible if top-account recovery is slower.
Lakshya'31 targets doubling revenue in five years (roughly 15% CAGR), with an inorganic component in the plan.
Margin: no target given; focus on cost optimisation under New Horizons, with the aim to expand margins over time while balancing growth.
Four reporting segments from Q1 FY27: BFSI, Technology/Media/Communication, Production, and Consumer.
Investor Day scheduled for 3 June 2026 in Mumbai.
capex_capacity: CBDT national direct tax analytics deal will have a longer transition period because of dependency on hardware delivery, which is taking longer than usual.
Two large deals announced early in FY26 are in the final stages of transition and ramp-up.
Headcount ended FY26 at 87,950; utilisation (ex-trainees) 85.7% in Q4.
Shift from a traditional delivery pyramid to a skill-based, role-driven workforce model.
Operations realigned into three lines of business: iRun (AI-enabled platformised operations), iTransform (platform, data and digital modernisation), and Business AI (new growth engine).
demand_pricing: FY26 order inflow USD 6.6bn; Q4 inflow USD 1.7bn; management described the pipeline as robust entering FY27.
Four of the six USD 100mn+ deals were renewals of competitors' contracts, per management; it said LTM has won more competitive renewals than it has lost.

Contract structure: core run/build contracts still 3-5 years; modernisation deals run for project duration; AI-adoption spend starts as projects and moves to long-term operations contracts, with FY27 expected to see acceleration.
Clients are asking for productivity and AI-infused innovation on existing contracts; management says it is delivering on these.
Management said the top BFSI account's productivity-led decline is done, with the AI productivity programme started in Q3 FY26.
Management flagged TCO of AI adoption as an emerging discussion point with clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are the top BFSI account's decline and the top-5 bucket drag bottoming out, and will the top five contribute to growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the BFSI account decline was deliberately pushed to bottom in Q4 and recovery should begin in Q1 FY27, but the recovery pace will be slower than the decline. Outside the top account, the business grew double digits in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins settle at around 16% or expand toward 17-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no specific margin target. It said cost optimisation and efficiency will continue under New Horizons, alongside growth, and that margin expansion remains the aim over time.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Lakshya strategy include a quantified growth target and are acquisitions part of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is to double revenue in five years, with an inorganic component. Acquisition priorities: capability acceleration, sovereign AI and security solutions in Europe, and client white spaces such as aerospace, defence and automotive in Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company competing more with consulting firms, and should it set up a BPS segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domain tech convergence is about technology applied in a domain context, not pure consulting. It set up a Business AI unit, which it does not classify as BPS because it is a new business model.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 TMC recovery and does it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Faster-than-expected ramp-up of a few SOWs with a top account in cloud acceleration drove the Q4 recovery. Management expects momentum to continue in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Why no FY27 growth guidance, given peers' muted outlooks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LTM does not give guidance. It is confident of full-year FY27 growth momentum, noting that one or two softer quarters are possible.

risks_watch: Recovery at the top BFSI account may lag its decline, and the speed of recovery is uncertain.
Top-two client concentration remains material; management says it will reduce concentration by growing other verticals.
Q4 margin fell to 15.1% after the partial wage hike from 1 January; watch whether FY27 productivity offsets it.
CBDT deal ramp-up is delayed by hardware delivery timelines.
Labour code exceptional item affected reported PAT in Q3 and Q4 FY26.
Watch Q1 FY27 segment reporting under the new four-segment structure, and the Investor Day on 3 June 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the Lakshya'31 strategy, but deliberately non-committal on numbers: management declined FY27 guidance and margin targets, and said recovery at the top BFSI account will be slower than the decline.
key_quotes: I am confident that we will continue our growth momentum for the full year of FY2027.
I am looking at doubling down the revenue in five years.
The total order inflow stood at USD 6.6 billion, representing a 10.3% year-over-year increase with a 300% increase in large deal wins, including six USD 100 million plus deals.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management expects FY26 growth momentum to carry into FY27 and targets doubling revenue in five years (~15% CAGR via Lakshya'31, including inorganic), backed by USD 6.6bn FY26 order inflow and steady USD 1.7bn Q4 inflow, but no specific capacity additions were given and utilisation fell to 85.7%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBIT margin fell 100bps QoQ to 15.1% from 16.1% on partial wage hike from 1 Jan, with no margin target given; management aims to expand margins over time via New Horizons cost optimisation, and FY27 productivity must offset the wage hike.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation (ex-trainees) was 85.7% in Q4 vs 86.9% in Q3 and no new plants or capacity additions were discussed; headcount ended FY26 at 87,950 with a net add of 3,643 YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects FY26 growth momentum (5.3% constant currency) to carry into FY27 and USD 6.6bn FY26 order inflow (+10.3% YoY) with steady USD 1.7bn Q4 inflow, though one or two softer quarters are possible if top-account recovery is slow.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; utilisation of 85.7% is high, but no board plan, land or approval was mentioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined numeric FY27 guidance, so there is no stated base to raise; it only says growth momentum should continue.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance exists to cut, but BFSI top account recovery will be slower than its decline (BFSI grew 3.7% in FY26) and one or two softer quarters are possible; CBDT deal ramp-up is delayed by hardware delivery.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Investor Day 3 June 2026 and Q1 FY27
rows.why: Business AI unit and three new lines of business (iRun, iTransform, Business AI) were set up, and Lakshya'31 targets doubling revenue in five years, but no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Top BFSI account recovery and large-deal ramp-up
rows.when: Q1 FY27 onward, slower than the decline
rows.why: Management said the top BFSI account decline bottomed in Q4 and recovery starts Q1 FY27, but BFSI grew only 3.7% in FY26 and two large deals announced early in FY26 are in final ramp-up stages.

rows.label: Lakshya'31 doubling revenue with inorganic component
rows.when: Over 5 years; inorganic moves possible within 2-4 quarters
rows.why: Target of doubling revenue in five years (~15% CAGR) with acquisition priorities in sovereign AI, security in Europe and aerospace/defence/automotive; Europe grew 12.4% in FY26 vs Americas 4.0%.

rows.label: Four-segment reporting and Investor Day
rows.why: Reporting moves to four segments (BFSI, TMC, Production, Consumer) from Q1 FY27 and the Investor Day is scheduled for 3 June 2026, which is a firm date.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 growth momentum, Lakshya'31 and the order book (USD 6.6bn), but cautious on numbers: no guidance, no margin target, and a slower top-BFSI recovery; analysts pushed on margins at 16% vs 17-18%, the top-account drag, and the AI/consulting competitive threat.
